name: rdt_source_random_state_corruption_data_scarce

source.paper: Tackling Data Corruption in Offline Reinforcement Learning via Sequence Modeling
source.scope: source corruption and downsampling semantics only; DT architecture/training remain this repository's frozen DT pipeline

corruption.rng_stream_rule: the same numpy RandomState instance first samples attack indices and then samples corruption noise, matching the public source implementation
corruption.std_reference: clean downsampled dataset observations before corruption
corruption.source_semantics: matches random observation corruption in utils/attack.py

normalization.rule: compute state_mean/state_std once from the clean downsampled dataset and reuse the same normalization for clean and all corrupted runs
normalization.reason: this repository's frozen DT pipeline normalizes states; holding clean downsampled normalization fixed isolates corruption from normalization drift
normalization.not_source_faithful: the public RDT DT baseline sets normalize=False by default

training.architecture_and_optimizer: unchanged from this repository's frozen vanilla DT

qualification_gate.degradation_definition: matched clean return for model seed minus corrupted return for corruption seed and model seed
qualification_gate.clean_compatibility_note: no full-data clean floor is imposed because this experiment intentionally changes to the paper's data-scarce regime

anti_tuning_rules: Do not change the 2 percent trajectory ratio after victim outcomes are observed.
Do not change the downsampling seed 1234 after victim outcomes are observed.
Do not change corruption rate 0.30 or corruption scale 1.0 after victim outcomes are observed.
Do not change corruption seeds 2023, 2024, 2025 after victim outcomes are observed.
Do not change from state corruption to another corruption field based on victim outcomes from this experiment.
Do not weaken the qualification gate after outcomes are observed.
Do not compare DT+MTM or RDT under this regime unless vanilla DT qualification passes.
claim_boundary: This is not an exact reproduction of the ICLR 2025 RDT baseline because this repository retains its own frozen DT architecture, optimizer, evaluation protocol, and state normalization convention.
The downsampling and random state-corruption mechanics are source-derived from the public RDT repository.
The purpose is to test whether a published corruption regime can produce stable degradation in this repository's vanilla DT before any defense comparison.
